content: When co-administered, the efficacy of microbiota oral therapy may be reduced due to pharmacodynamic antagonism caused by certain antibacterial agents. It is recommended to complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days prior to initiating microbiota oral therapy. Microbiota oral formulations contain bacterial spores, and their effectiveness can be compromised if administered alongside antibacterial agents. Specific antibacterial agents, such as sulopenem, etzadroxil/probenecid, tebipenem, tedizolid, telavancin, tetracycline, tigecycline, tobramycin, trimethoprim, and vancomycin, have been shown to decrease the effects of microbiota oral therapy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. In such cases, alternative drugs should be considered or co-administration should be avoided. Microbiota-based live biotherapeutics are delivered orally to introduce a diverse consortium of microbes into the gut, aiming to reduce recurrent Clostridioides difficile infections following antibiotic treatment. Each dose, typically consisting of four capsules, should be taken on an empty stomach before the first meal of the day. The product should be stored in its original packaging at temperatures between 2°C and 25°C (36°F to 77°F) and should not be frozen. There is no available data on the use of microbiota oral therapy in pregnant women, and developmental toxicity studies in animals have not been conducted. It is also unknown whether the product is excreted in human milk, and there is no information to assess its effects on breastfed infants or milk production. The above information is provided for general educational purposes. Formulary information may vary and is subject to change. For the most current details, contact the applicable plan provider.
